regions.full_page: I am sending the original of this carbon to Miss Lyke. I hope it may smoothe the thing off in a manner; though I am not just clear as to what she really com- plains about. Perhaps she expected a personal acknow- ledgement of somekind more than just a rubber-stamp. I've been getting so many cheques - bothe here at St. Felix and at St. Michael's that I would have to posess an extraordinary memory to recollect particulars like this little mixup might require. One thing I do remem- ber, that during the nine or ten months I was at St. Michael's it was very seldom, if ever, that I was with- out letters to acknowledge, even though I sometimes worked on them till after min-night. God be praised, however, I did not mind it and my health kept fine. Seomtimes my two faithful ole sentinels would threaten to go on strike and to quiet them down I felt I'd have to give it up. Well she will possibly writ again. Afer all if she got her check back, she ought to know that things were oky .. ? We'll hope for the best anyhow and pray for the dear Lord's gentle guidence. Praying in the mean time for one anothers' conversion - till some day we can sin no more and the good angels will be able to bear us off to the eternity; forever - really and truly CONVERTED, WE'LL sing on withe angels awaiting that blessed day: "0 all ye works of the Lord bless the Lord, Praise and exalt Him above all forever."
